issues.title: Perfect HT: up to 8 replicas, largest power of two that fits the cap
issues.hypothesis: PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY is still 1.13s CPU (second largest operator) for ~470M state updates. E0003 (K=4 replicas) cut 12.3% by breaking same-state read-modify-write chains. E0005 made each aggregate's update a tight typed loop, so store-to-load forwarding latency on the same state address is now a larger share of each iteration. In q01 one group holds 49% of rows: with K=4, row i and row i+4 hit the same state ~half the time, so the chain is still only 4 rows long. K=8 doubles the independent chains. Also, the current code (perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp:44) drops straight to replica_count=1 when total_groups*tuple_size*4 exceeds the 1MiB cap. Choosing the largest power of two that fits keeps some replication for mid-sized domains.
issues.plan: In src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp: set MAX_REPLICA_COUNT (line 10) to 8. In the constructor (~line 36-45), when can_replicate, start at MAX_REPLICA_COUNT and halve while total_groups*tuple_size*replica_count > MAX_REPLICATED_HT_SIZE and replica_count > 1. The replica mask at line 312 (replica_count-1) already assumes a power of two; keep that invariant. Check that CombineReplicas and the Scan-time fold loop over replica_count rather than a hard-coded 4 (grep for 4 or MAX_REPLICA_COUNT in the replica loops). No other changes. Bench q01 several times; if K=8 is not better than K=4 beyond noise, try K=8 with the fallback only, or report neutral.
issues.expected_gain: q01 2-5% (HT CPU 1.13s -> ~0.95s if the chains are the remaining bottleneck).
issues.generality: Any perfect-hash group-by with few groups and skewed or low-cardinality keys (common in reporting queries). The halving fallback also helps mid-sized group domains that currently get no replication. Possible slowdown: Init/Combine/fold costs scale with 8x states, which is negligible for tiny domains, and the extra cache footprint is bounded by the 1MiB cap.
issues.risk: Low. The semantics are unchanged because replication is already gated on order-independent, non-DISTINCT aggregates. The only correctness hazard is a replica loop that hard-codes 4.

issues.title: Investigate per-value cost of bitpacked int64 scans
issues.hypothesis: Measured with EXPLAIN ANALYZE: sum(l_quantity) alone has TABLE_SCAN 0.67s CPU for 60M values (~11ns/value), sum(l_extendedprice) 1.07s (~18ns/value), and 4 bitpacked decimal columns 2.04s. The FOR bitpacking unpack (fastpforlib Unroller, 32 values per call) plus ApplyFrameOfReference should cost ~1ns/value. The overhead is either elsewhere in the scan path (ColumnData::ScanVector, GetVectorScanType, HasUpdates locks, FetchUpdates, validity scan, per-32-value dispatch in BitpackingScanPartial at bitpacking.cpp:775), or the machine's threads are oversubscribed. The wider column is slower, which suggests that the unpack or memory traffic, not fixed per-vector overhead, dominates.
issues.plan: Investigation first: compare scan CPU of an INT64 bitpacked column with different widths, and with threads=1 vs 8, to separate machine effects from code. If unpack dominates, add an int64 fast path in BitpackingScanPartial that, for a full metadata-group-aligned FOR run, unpacks and applies the frame of reference in one fused loop over 32-value blocks (avoiding the switch dispatch per block and the second pass).
issues.expected_gain: Unknown until measured; scan is ~60% of q01 CPU.
issues.generality: Every scan of bitpacked integer/decimal columns.
issues.risk: Medium; needs measurement before any code.

dispatch: Perfect HT: up to 8 replicas, largest power of two that fits the cap
output.memory:
# Memory

## Workload
- Single visible template q01 = TPC-H Q1 shape: scan lineitem with one range filter on a date (selects ~98%),
  4 groups (2 string keys -> compressed to utinyint), 4 sum_no_overflow + 3 avg + count_star on DECIMAL(int64).
- Bench ~298ms after E0005 (profile). Operator CPU: TABLE_SCAN 2.09s, PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 1.13s,
  projections 0.19 + 0.04 + 0.18s.
- Storage: l_quantity/extendedprice/discount/tax/shipdate = BitPacking (FOR mode); returnflag/linestatus = old Dictionary.
- Group distribution: N,O 49%, A,F 25%, R,F 25%, N,F <1%, randomly interleaved.

## Key measurements (dbe-tool sql EXPLAIN ANALYZE, single runs, noisy)
- sum(l_quantity) alone: wall 0.102s, scan CPU 0.67s (~11ns/value!). sum(l_extendedprice): 0.150s, scan 1.07s.
  4 decimal sums, no filter: 0.291s wall, scan 2.04s. Wider bit width -> slower. Unexplained: unpack should be ~1ns/value.
  Not yet known whether this is the machine (WSL2, maybe oversubscribed threads) or the code. Next step: threads=1 vs 8.
- Q1 with filter ~680ms vs no filter + max(shipdate) ~555ms in early rounds; the filter column scan is ~60-70ms of it.
- count(*) with only the date filter: 71ms.
- Decimal multiply already drops its overflow check via stats (arithmetic.cpp PropagateNumericStats ~l.174-184),
  so the projections are not doing overflow checks.

## Codebase facts
- Scan with filters: RowGroup::Scan (src/storage/table/row_group.cpp ~694-829). Filter cols -> ColumnData::Filter
  (Scan + ToUnifiedFormat + FilterSelection). Other cols -> compression select, else Scan + Slice(sel).
- ColumnData::ScanVector / GetVectorScanType / FetchUpdates take update_lock per vector (column_data.cpp:54, 121, 266).
- Bitpacking scan: BitpackingScanPartial (bitpacking.cpp:775). Per 32 values: UnPackBlock (switch on width ->
  fastpforlib Unroller, scalar) + ApplyFrameOfReference pass. No bitpacking filter/select callbacks.
- Perfect hash agg: src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp. MAX_REPLICA_COUNT l.10, MAX_REPLICATED_HT_SIZE 1MiB l.12,
  replica choice l.36-45 (falls to 1 if 4x does not fit), replica mask l.312 (needs a power of two). E0005 typed fused loops in AddChunk.
- sum_no_overflow: extension/core_functions/aggregate/distributive/sum.cpp. avg stats rewrite: avg.cpp (E0004).
- dbe-tool sql: typeof(col) needs an aggregate wrapper. EXPLAIN ANALYZE works; pipe through grep is allowed.
  Read the .dbe files with the Read tool (cd plus head is blocked).

## Round log
- G1R1: E0001 per-group simple_update -> RETIRED (bad idea: groups interleaved).
- G1R2: E0002 bitpacking select (flat compacted payload) -> RETIRED: neutral. Slicing is not the cost.
- G1R3: E0003 perfect HT replicas K=4 -> ACCEPTED -12.3%.
- G1R4: E0004 avg int64 state via stats -> ACCEPTED -5.1%.
- G1R5: E0005 fused typed update loops for sum/avg/count_star in perfect HT -> ACCEPTED -5.9% (1.277x).
  Row-wise fusion (all aggregates per row, with a switch) was 34% SLOWER; keep column-at-a-time typed loops.
- G1R6: dispatched K=8 replicas with a halving fallback to fit the 1MiB cap.

## Directions
- Promising: perfect-HT micro-work (replicas, typed loops) gave reliable wins. Extending the E0005 fast path to
  count(x), min/max, double sum/avg would generalise it (more aggregate mixes take the fast path).
- Biggest open target: the scan at 11-18ns/value for bitpacked int64 (see the investigation issue). Measure before coding.
- Fuse stacked projections (0.4s CPU): needs optimizer investigation (compressed_materialization).
- Exhausted: per-group partitioning (E0001), flat select output (E0002), decimal overflow checks (already removed by stats).
